entry: Conflict between the [[Russian Empire]] and [[Empire of Japan|Japan]], 1904–1905. Fought over rival imperial ambitions in [[Manchuria]] and Korea, the war began when Japan launched a surprise attack on the Russian Pacific Fleet at Port Arthur on February 9, 1904. Japanese forces took Port Arthur in January 1905 and captured Mukden, the Manchurian capital, that March. At sea, the Japanese Combined Fleet destroyed Russia's Baltic Fleet at the Battle of Tsushima in May 1905, after its voyage of more than seven months and 18,000 nautical miles. The Treaty of Portsmouth, mediated by U.S. president [[Theodore Roosevelt]], recognized Japanese interests in Korea and transferred Russia's Liaodong Peninsula lease and the southern half of [[Sakhalin]] to Japan. The defeat of a European power by an Asian one surprised observers and transformed the global balance of power. The humiliating defeat contributed to unrest culminating in the 1905 Russian Revolution.

War between the [[Ottoman Empire]] and a Russian-led coalition, 1877–1878. The coalition also included Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro. Russia sought to recover territory lost in the [[Crimean War]], reassert itself on the [[Black Sea]], and support Balkan nations seeking to free themselves from Ottoman rule. Russian-led forces pushed the Ottomans back to the gates of [[Constantinople]], drawing intervention from the Western European great powers. Russia claimed the Caucasian provinces of Kars and Batum and annexed the Budjak region. Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro formally proclaimed independence, and Bulgaria emerged as an autonomous state with Russian support. The [[Congress of Berlin]] in 1878 revised the terms, reducing Bulgaria's territory and returning some Macedonian land to Ottoman control. [[Greece]] annexed parts of Thessaly and Arta. The war's human cost exceeded 250,000 deaths.

Phase of the Russo-Ukrainian War since 2022. [[Russia]] invaded Ukraine on February 24, 2022, beginning the largest and deadliest war in Europe since [[World War II]], an escalation of a conflict that began in 2014. The fighting has caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties. Russia occupies roughly 20% of Ukraine, and about 8 million Ukrainians have been displaced within the country. Russia's 2022 annexation of four partly occupied provinces was internationally condemned. The [[International Criminal Court]] has issued arrest warrants for [[Vladimir Putin]] and five other Russian officials.

Armed conflict between Russia and Ukraine, begun in 2014 and ongoing. Russia occupied and annexed [[Crimea]] in March 2014 after a referendum described as illegitimate. Russian-backed separatists then seized parts of the [[Donbas]] and proclaimed the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics, starting the Donbas war. The conflict became a static, [[Trench warfare|trench-style]] war, and the Minsk II agreements of February 2015 were never fully implemented. Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022 began the current phase. The [[International Criminal Court]] judged the conflict both a national and an international armed conflict involving Russia.

Region of the northern United States affected by industrial decline. Common definitions include Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, [[Ohio]], Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. It was the industrial heartland from the late 19th century through the late 20th, built on iron and steel, automobiles, and coal. Decline began in the 1950s and 1960s as coal demand fell and steel faced competition from [[Germany]] and [[Japan]]. Factories relocated to the Sun Belt or overseas, and families left, leaving cities with falling tax revenues and abandoned buildings. The name, derived from [[Rust|rust]], refers to the corrosive effects of decline.

Mixture of iron oxides formed when [[Iron|iron]] reacts with [[Oxygen|oxygen]] in the presence of water or air moisture. It ranges in color from red-orange to reddish-brown. Its main compounds are iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) and iron(III) oxide-hydroxide (FeO(OH)). Surface rust is flaky and friable and gives no protection to the iron beneath, unlike the stable oxide layers of [[Aluminium|aluminum]], copper, and tin. Rusting is the common term for [[Corrosion|corrosion]] of iron and its alloys such as [[Steel|steel]]. [[Chloride]] ions, as in saltwater, speed the process, and the brittle oxide reduces the strength of the object.

Root vegetable (*Brassica napus*) known as swede in Britain and much of the Commonwealth and as rutabaga in North America. It arose as a hybrid of cabbage (*B. oleracea*) and turnip (*B. rapa*) and is related to rapeseed. The roots are eaten in many ways, and the leaves and tops feed livestock. The first known printed reference, by Swiss botanist Gaspard Bauhin in 1620, describes it growing wild in Sweden. It was probably bred in northern Europe around the 16th century. It reached England from Germany around 1750, according to one account, Scotland around 1781, and North America in the early 19th century. Rutabaga became a food of last resort in Germany and France during World War I and World War II, when boiled rutabaga stew was a typical meal during shortages.

Dutch actor with more than 170 roles over nearly 50 years. His career began in 1969 with the title role in the Dutch television series *Floris*, and he gained international recognition with *Soldier of Orange* (1977) and *Spetters* (1980). He then moved into American films, notably as the self-aware replicant Roy Batty in *Blade Runner* (1982). Later he took supporting roles in *Batman Begins* (2005) and *Sin City* (2005) and returned to Dutch cinema, winning the 2012 Rembrandt Award for Best Actor. He supported environmentalist causes and founded an AIDS awareness organization.

American jurist and associate justice of the [[Supreme Court of the United States|U.S. Supreme Court]] (1993–2020). Nominated by President [[Bill Clinton]], she was the first Jewish woman and the second woman on the Court, after Sandra Day O'Connor. Earlier she co-founded the Women's Rights Project of the American Civil Liberties Union and argued six gender-discrimination cases before the Supreme Court, winning five. Her majority opinions included *United States v. Virginia* (1996), which invalidated the Virginia Military Institute's male-only admissions policy. She died of [[Pancreatic cancer|pancreatic cancer]] at 87, and Amy Coney Barrett filled her vacancy.

Rare transition metal of the [[Platinum|platinum]] group, symbol Ru, atomic number 44. Like other platinum-group metals, ruthenium is unreactive to most chemicals. Russian scientist Karl Ernst Claus, of Baltic-German ancestry, discovered it in 1844 at [[Kazan]] State University and named it for Ruthenia, the Latin name for Russia. Ruthenium usually occurs as a minor component of platinum ores, and annual production rose from about 19 tonnes in 2009 to 35.5 tonnes in 2017. Most of it goes into wear-resistant electrical contacts and thick-film resistors. Small amounts harden platinum and palladium and markedly increase the corrosion resistance of [[Titanium|titanium]]. It also serves as a chemical catalyst and as a capping layer for extreme-ultraviolet photomasks in semiconductor lithography. Its ores are mined in the [[Ural Mountains]], North and South America, Sudbury, [[Ontario]], and [[South Africa]].

19th U.S. president (1877–1881) and a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] from [[Ohio]]. A Union Army officer in the Civil War, he was wounded five times and rose to brevet major general. He lost the popular vote to Democrat Samuel J. Tilden, but a congressional commission awarded him disputed electoral votes. An 1877 arrangement reportedly ended federal support for Reconstruction, though the existence of such a deal remains disputed. As president he called in the U.S. Army to end the Great Railroad Strike of 1877, which remains the deadliest conflict between workers and strikebreakers in American history. Historians rank him below average to average.

Landmark experiments that showed atoms have a dense, positively charged nucleus. Performed from 1906 to 1913 at the University of Manchester by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden under [[Ernest Rutherford]], they fired [[Alpha particle|alpha particles]] at thin metal foil and measured how the beams scattered. The results showed that all of an atom's positive charge and most of its mass are concentrated in a central nucleus. [[J. J. Thomson|Thomson]]'s earlier model had spread positive charge through a sphere, but the data fit single scattering from a compact central charge. Rutherford explained the effect in a 1911 paper, which led to the widespread use of scattering to study subatomic matter. The paper also led to the planetary Rutherford model of the atom and, eventually, the [[Bohr model]].

Landlocked country in East Africa, with its capital at [[Kigali]]. Rwanda is bordered by Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, and the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. Its roughly 14 million people make it the 21st most densely populated country in the world. Tutsi kings built a centralized kingdom from the mid-18th century. Germany colonized Rwanda in 1897 as part of German East Africa, and Belgium took control in 1916. A Hutu revolt in 1959 led to an independent Hutu-dominated republic in 1962. After a 1973 coup, the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) launched a civil war in 1990, and the [[Rwandan genocide|1994 genocide]] ended with the RPF's military victory that July. Since then the RPF has governed as a de facto one-party state under [[Paul Kagame]], president since 2000. The economy relies on services, [[Coffee|coffee]] and tea, and tourism, and the country belongs to the [[African Union]] and the [[Commonwealth of Nations]].

Campaign of systematic killing of Tutsi, and some moderate Hutu and Twa, in [[Rwanda]] from April 7 to July 19, 1994. Hutu militias killed over roughly 100 days, and victims were often murdered by their neighbors. Most scholarly estimates put the number of Tutsi dead at 500,000 to 662,000, while the Rwandan Constitution states that over one million people were killed. Between 250,000 and 500,000 rapes were committed. The killings followed the April 6 assassination of President Juvénal Habyarimana, as Hutu extremists used the power vacuum to target Tutsi and moderate Hutu leaders. The international community did not intervene to stop the killings. The Rwandan Patriotic Front ended the genocide by capturing government-held territory in July 1994. Many perpetrators and Hutu refugees fled into [[Zaire]], now the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], contributing to the First Congo War in 1996.

Japanese writer, regarded as the "father of the Japanese [[Short story|short story]]." Active in the Taishō period, he studied English literature at Tokyo Imperial University, now the [[University of Tokyo]], from 1913 and began writing as a student. His story "Rashōmon" (1915), based on a twelfth-century tale, was not well received by his friends. [[Natsume Sōseki]], whom he admired, praised his next story, "Hana" (1916), and brought him fame. Works such as "Hell Screen" (1918) explore artistic obsession and the supernatural. In 1950 [[Akira Kurosawa]] adapted "Rashōmon" into the film *Rashōmon*, which won the Grand Prix at the Venice Film Festival. Japan's premier literary award, the Akutagawa Prize, is named after him. He died by suicide at 35.

Welsh footballer and manager who spent his entire playing career at Manchester United. A left midfielder or winger, he made a club record 963 competitive appearances and won 13 [[Premier League]] titles, more than any other player. His honors include two [[UEFA Champions League]] titles and four FA Cups. He holds the Premier League record for assists, with 162. Giggs captained the Great Britain team at the 2012 Summer Olympics and managed Wales from 2018 until resigning in 2022. He was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 2007 for services to football.

Canadian actor, singer, and musician. Known for both independent films and studio features, he has received [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations for *Half Nelson*, *La La Land*, and *Barbie*, the last being his highest-grossing release. His leading roles have grossed over US$4 billion worldwide. Early work included the [[Disney Channel]] series *The All New Mickey Mouse Club*, and he gained acclaim in *The Notebook*, *Drive*, and *Blue Valentine*. He made his directorial debut with the fantasy film *Lost River* (2014).

American writer, director, and producer, working mainly in television. He signed what was described as the largest development deal in television history with [[Netflix]]. His series include *Nip/Tuck* (2003–2010), *Glee* (2009–2015), *American Horror Story*, *Pose*, and *9-1-1*. His accolades include six Primetime Emmy Awards and a Tony Award. He directed film adaptations of *Running with Scissors* (2006) and *The Normal Heart* (2014). Critics have questioned the accuracy of his true-crime dramas, including the *Monsters* anthology, which the Menendez family criticized.

Canadian-American actor, entrepreneur, and film producer, born and raised in [[Vancouver]]. Known for comedic and superhero films, he was the world's second-highest-paid actor in 2020 and 2024. He achieved his greatest commercial success as the title character of the *Deadpool* films, with *Deadpool & Wolverine* (2024) his highest-grossing release. His films as a leading actor have grossed $6.6 billion worldwide. He holds an ownership stake in Mint Mobile and co-owns the Welsh soccer club Wrexham. He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 2017.

Irish ultra-low-cost airline, the largest in Europe by scheduled passengers. Founded in 1984 by Christopher and Tony Ryan, it is headquartered in Swords, County [[Dublin]], and operates a no-frills model. Nearly one-third of its income comes from ancillary fees for seats, baggage, and check-in. In 2025 it sold 208 million tickets, averaging €70 in revenue against €62 in costs per ticket. Its fleet is standardized on [[Boeing 737]] aircraft. The airline consistently scores poorly in customer-satisfaction surveys, results the company dismisses as statistically unrepresentative.

Cereal grass (*Secale cereale*) grown for grain, forage, and cover. Rye tolerates cold weather and poor soil better than other cereals, so it is grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia. It belongs to the wheat tribe with [[Wheat|wheat]] and [[Barley|barley]]. It probably reached Europe as a minor admixture in wheat fields before being cultivated in its own right. Its grain is used for [[Bread|bread]], beer, rye whiskey, and fodder. Rye was a staple in Scandinavia during the [[Middle Ages]], and rye crispbread remains popular there. Europe produces about half the world's rye, and little is traded between countries. A wheat-rye hybrid, triticale, is grown in large quantities worldwide.

Island chain stretching southwest from [[Kyushu]] toward [[Taiwan]], also called the Nansei Islands. The northern Satsunan Islands belong to Kagoshima Prefecture, and the southern islands to [[Okinawa Prefecture]]. The larger islands are mostly volcanic and the smaller mostly coral, and [[Okinawa Island]] is the largest. The climate ranges from humid subtropical in the north to tropical rainforest in the south, with heavy rain affected by the rainy season and [[Typhoon|typhoons]]. The islands were held by the United States after the 1951 Treaty of San Francisco and returned to Japan under the 1971 Okinawa reversion agreement, with China disputing the Senkaku Islands.

German multinational enterprise-software company based in Walldorf. Founded in 1972 by five former [[IBM]] engineers, it is the world's largest vendor of enterprise software, with offices in 78 countries and 110,000 employees. Its first commercial product, the RF financial accounting system, launched in 1973, and SAP R/2 followed in 1979. In June 2025 it was the largest European company by market capitalization. SAP is a component of the DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 indices. Its S/4HANA enterprise resource planning platform runs on the in-memory SAP HANA database.

Positive-sense RNA betacoronavirus that causes COVID-19. First identified in [[Wuhan]], China, it is related to SARS-CoV-1, which caused the 2002–2004 SARS outbreak. Its closest known relative is a bat coronavirus, and its genetic similarity to bat viruses suggests zoonotic origin, though the route of transmission to humans remains under research. The virus spreads mainly through close contact and through aerosols and respiratory droplets. It enters human cells by binding to the ACE2 receptor. The [[World Health Organization]] declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern from January 30, 2020, to May 5, 2023.

Flash [[Memory card|memory card]] format used in portable electronics. Introduced in August 1999 as Secure Digital by SanDisk, Panasonic, and Kioxia, it succeeded MultiMediaCard and added digital rights management and a mechanical write-protect switch. The nonprofit SD Association, founded in January 2000, develops its specifications; it had about 1,000 member companies as of 2023. Full-size, miniSD (now obsolete), and microSD cards are used in digital cameras, camcorders, [[Video game console|video game consoles]], [[Mobile phone|mobile phones]], and drones. Capacity classes include SDHC, SDXC, and SDUC.
